social_circle.name: Daniel Lewis

demographics.occupation: Retired high school math teacher; tutors students from home and volunteers at the Morton Grove Public Library
demographics.education: Bachelor's in mathematics; Illinois teaching certificate

background.how_they_met: Met at a Chicago Cubs game in 1989; she was working as a QC technician, he was a high school math teacher.
background.why_close: Spouse of 35 years; they navigated infertility, both parents' end-of-life care, his retirement adjustment, and the recent loss of Nicole's longtime client together. Daniel is the person Nicole leans on most — he made beef stew the week Mr. Henderson died and watched 'Schindler's List' with her. Their relationship runs on quiet daily reliability rather than drama.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in complete sentences with proper punctuation, no emoji, sometimes uses dashes the way he uses chalkboard logic. Short and practical during the day ('picked up Winston's pills'), warmer in the evening. Drops the occasional dry one-liner.

shared_activities: Weekday morning routine (her 6:15am dog walk, his weekend breakfast cooking)
Every-other-Sunday family dinner hosting with Karen and Tom
First-Sunday-of-month monthly budget review
Early voting together at village hall
Annual Oregon/Vermont/Napa-style road trips and the saved-for Kyoto 2031 trip
9:30am Sunday mass at Saint Martha's
recent_text_topics: Logistics about Winston: vet appointment confirmations, whether he's eaten, who's home for the 4pm walk.
Coordinating around her geriatric care management coursework block (7:30–8:30pm weeknights) — he handles dishes/dog those nights.
Grocery list pings from Mariano's; she texts him to add things she forgot, he sometimes asks her to grab library-pickup snacks.
Property tax escrow check-ins ahead of the August installment.
Updates from her drive home — traffic on Dempster, whether she's stopping at the parish for bereavement-ministry drop-offs.
Quiet check-ins after the Mr. Henderson loss in February — he still asks how she's doing on Fridays.
Long-thread planning for their 35th anniversary in June and the Kyoto-2031 sub-account update each month.

social_circle.name: Megan Brennan

demographics.occupation: Assistant public defender, Dane County Public Defender's Office
demographics.education: B.A. political science, University of Wisconsin–Madison; J.D., University of Wisconsin Law School

background.how_they_met: Family — Megan is the daughter of Daniel's sister Karen and her husband Tom. Nicole has known her since birth.
background.why_close: Nicole sees herself in Megan — both like systems, both are mission-driven helpers. Megan lived with Nicole and Daniel for a summer during college. She calls Nicole 'Aunt Nicole' and treats her like a second mother. They keep a standing first-Sunday-of-the-month FaceTime, and Megan has nudged Nicole's politics leftward on criminal-justice issues (the $100 Wisconsin public defender donation came from her).

interests: true-crime podcasts (which she sends Nicole and Nicole ignores)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in lowercase, fragments, plenty of emoji (🌱☕😭). Sends long voice notes after court days. Frequently shares articles with a 'thoughts??' tag. Uses 'omg' and 'literally' often.

shared_activities: First-Sunday-of-month FaceTime
Easter and Christmas visits to Morton Grove (Megan and Jess)
Occasional Madison visits by Nicole and Daniel
Sharing reading recommendations (Megan was the one who pushed Isabel Wilkerson on her)
Coordinating donations to legal-aid funds Megan vets
recent_text_topics: Megan venting about a tough case she can't fully describe, asking Nicole to just listen.
Therapist scheduling friction — Megan switching weekly slots; Nicole gently checking in that she's still going.
A long thread debating whether Megan and Jess should come for Nicole and Daniel's 35th anniversary weekend in June.
Megan forwarding a New Yorker piece on indigent defense and asking 'have you read this'.
Garden updates from Nicole (first tomato seedlings transplanted in late April); Megan sending photos of her own balcony herbs.
Coordinating the Mother's Day card and call rotation with Karen (Karen and Tom in Glenview, Nicole as the aunt who actually answers texts).
Megan asking eldercare questions on Karen's behalf — Karen has been worrying out loud about her own knees and Megan funnels it to Nicole.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05 ('a wonderful niece — Daniel's sister Karen has a daughter named Megan who just turned twenty-eight and lives in Madison. She calls me Aunt Nicole and we have a standing FaceTime on the first Sunday of each month'), Q05 ('She's a public defender in Madison... She and her partner Jess came down for Easter'), Q11 ('my niece Megan lived with us one summer in college'), Q29 ('Megan pointed me to a Wisconsin public defender support fund. I gave a hundred dollars'), Q30 ('Megan is openly active — she's a public defender, this is her life's work'), Q46 ('Megan deals with secondary trauma from her caseload but she has a therapist she sees regularly').

social_circle.name: Linda Petrowski

demographics.occupation: Senior quality assurance analyst at a mid-size pharmaceutical company in Des Plaines

background.how_they_met: Met in the early 1990s when both worked at the same small Skokie pharmaceutical lab.
background.why_close: Their friendship survived Nicole leaving the lab in 2009 because they deliberately put an every-other-Thursday lunch at The Cottage on the calendar fifteen years ago and have not broken it. Linda is the friend Nicole talks to about everything except politics — Linda is more conservative and they've learned to steer around it.

interests: competitive crossword solving (she and Nicole sometimes race on the NYT app)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Long texts written like emails, signs off with her initial 'L'. Rarely uses emoji except a 🙄 or 😂. Will send a one-word 'Thursday?' to confirm their standing lunch.

shared_activities: Every-other-Thursday lunch at The Cottage in Park Ridge (15+ years)
NYT crossword solve-offs
Occasional weekend antique-fair drives
Annual joint birthday dinner (their birthdays are six weeks apart)
Mutual sounding-board on aging-parent / aging-self stuff
recent_text_topics: Confirming the next Thursday lunch and where to sit (Linda has Opinions about the booth by the window).
Nicole asked Linda how she's recovering from her own knee scope last fall; comparing cortisone-shot notes after Nicole's February injection.
Linda complaining about her sons not calling enough; Nicole letting her vent without trying to fix it.
A long back-and-forth about whether they should finally do a weekend trip to Galena — Linda has been pushing it for two years.
Crossword Saturday: Linda texts 'STUMPED ON 32 ACROSS' midmorning.
Linda gently teasing Nicole for buying yet more yarn from the Northbrook shop.
Avoiding the news together — they have a tacit agreement to skip political topics, which they explicitly named again last month.
